rationale.conceptual: The core method is a basic feedforward neural network (two hidden layers, ReLU, dropout, early stopping) used for regression on spectral data. There is no novel algorithm or deep theoretical derivation; the challenge lies in correctly implementing the described architecture and experimental protocol, not in understanding complex machine learning concepts.
rationale.execution: The pipeline involves nine distinct stages: dataset preprocessing, training a baseline model, creating three series of size-filtered training subsets (blue/green/brown for n=12-20), training ~30 models, generating noisy spectra with five λ values, evaluating all cross-combinations of training/test noise and smoothing, and training augmentation models. This many serial steps and model training runs makes the orchestration non-trivial, though each individual step uses standard libraries and is well-defined.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper applies a standard feedforward neural network to predict ground-state PDOS from core-loss spectra. The conceptual challenge is low because the ML method is a textbook FNN with dropout and early stopping; domain-specific knowledge about spectroscopy is secondary to the code reproduction. Execution is moderately complex: a multi-stage pipeline training many models (baseline, extrapolation series, noise-robustness matrix, augmentation) on a small public dataset. Each step is straightforward but requires careful implementation of the described protocol. Resource needs are minimal: models are small, dataset is tiny (~22k molecules, 160 input bins), and no GPU is necessary. The discipline is computational chemistry applied to materials spectroscopy.

compute_estimate.reasoning: The models are small (input 160, hidden 160/120, output 300) and the dataset contains only ~22k molecules with 160-bin spectra; training is feasible on CPU, though many models are trained. Peak RAM would be a few GB for loading the dataset and training one model at a time. Data size is under 1 GB (spectra and PDOS arrays).
